Acute 300-micrometre slices were recorded at 32-34 degrees C, with RGL voltage clamp at -65 mV and 5 mM kynurenic acid. The internal solution is ambiguously printed as 135 mM CsCl gluconate. Clamp-current sign does not directly identify native membrane polarization, spiking or cell-cycle entry.

Population experiments use five consecutive days of stimulation, eight hours per day: ChR2 blue light at 472 nm, 5-ms pulses at 8 Hz for 30 seconds every five minutes, or continuous 593-nm eNpHR light. On day five, EdU is injected intraperitoneally at 41.1 mg/kg six times, two hours apart, with collection two hours after the last injection. Repeated injections are not independent replicates. Population scoring uses 40-micrometre sections, every sixth section, and nestin-positive inverted-Y morphology over an EdU- or MCM2-positive nucleus. At two and seven days after induction, one GFP-positive RGL is classified as a quiescent clone and two or more nuclei as an activated clone. These are fixed-tissue, spatially assigned clones using a referenced method, not live observations of every division or independently verified common ancestry. studies.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence or proof of no pathway contribution. The corticosterone null is a two-hour circulating concentration, not complete exclusion of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal mediation. Extended Data 3 reuses the Figure 2c saline/LPS data; it is not an independent replication.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.
